text:
Maddy: Kicking off BrightBridge POC ramp. Demo scheduled 17:00 PT. Customer is seeing intermittent 401s and bursts of 429s when traffic hits ~20 TPS. Need triage + ETA. @Ravi @Elena @Priya please.

Ravi: Oncall — looking now. 401s vs 429s suggests both auth failures and throttling. Can you paste a sample request/response and any headers?

Maddy: Sample curl from customer:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response snippet:
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key"}
Also seeing rate headers in other requests: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 100`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`

Diego: Customer uses an auth proxy that mints short-lived tokens for each session. Could be proxy misconfig or key rotation.

Elena: Infra: I see token introspection fails in our logs at 2026-11-03T14:52:12Z. Log dump (sanitized):
```
2026-11-03T14:52:12Z request_id=rb-7f3a client_ip=54.12.34.56 path=/v1/generate status=401 err="invalid_api_key" token_id=tok-sess-9f2
2026-11-03T14:52:13Z request_id=rb-7f3b client_ip=54.12.34.56 path=/v1/generate status=429 err="rate_limit_exceeded" X-RateLimit-Remaining=0
```

Priya: Security: 401s with short-lived tokens often come from JWKS fetch failures or clock skew. Any recent proxy upgrade?

Maddy: They rolled auth-proxy to v2.0 yesterday morning. Attaching their proxy log: token fetch to our introspect endpoint returning 502 for a handful of requests.

Ravi: For immediate mitigation I see two paths: 1) temporary rotate to a long-lived server-side API key for the demo, and client-side throttle to avoid bursts OR 2) bump their customer rate-limit for the POC and enable a short-term permissive token grace window. Option 1 is safer and quicker.

Elena: We can bump per-customer pipeline limits for the trial to 250 TPS on the Dedicated pool. Doing the change now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: applied config change customer=brightbridge rate_limit=250 by infra at 2026-11-03T15:01:03Z

Maddy: Thanks — can you confirm if 401s clear after they switch to the server key?

Ravi: 401s dropped by ~90% after they moved to server key. 429s still appear briefly during warm-up because of KV cache misses on the model side. I pushed a caching tweak to reduce cold-start tokenization cost.

Diego: I'm updating the POC runbook and messaging to BrightBridge: please use server key for demo window and rotate afterwards. Also they asked about cost for higher bursts — @Sara can you handle pricing?

Sara: I'll waive extra burst fees for the POC. Will send a one-page amendment and note the exception for demo keys.

Priya: Security sign-off for server-key usage is granted for demo only. Constraint: rotate key within 24h and add a one-time exception in RB-459.

Maddy: Customer reports the demo flow is green now. Thank you all. We'll do a short postmortem: add token-introspection alerts, detect proxy JWKS failures, and add proxy version to onboarding checklist.

Elena: Filing INF-2026 to auto-detect JWKS/introspection failures and alert the SRE team.

Ravi: I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and mitigations, and link the infra and security tickets. Closing this swarm unless anyone needs to keep it open. :thumbsup:

Diego: Great work team. Noting follow-ups: runbook update, pricing amendment, post-demo key rotation.

Maddy: Closing — will DM follow-ups to stakeholders. :lock: :eyes:
